title: Dupuy 155
contents: The Tuscan ambassador and Don Juan discuss neutral custody of Chateau d'If. The Grand Duke cannot compel Bussetto or surrender the Italian garrison's position without breaking his promise.
status: 2/9 pages transcribed; 1 more in part; 2/9 pages deciphered; 1 more in part
fields: Ferdinando I de Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany
41 codes: 20 letter signs, 19 in nomenclature, 2 unidentified
Interlinear Italian plaintext on the same pages.
Different volume: Dupuy 63, f48 (23 April 1597). Cryptiana's reconstructed key

excerpt: **[ante]cessore et nel mio. Et se Vostra Altezza nel principio fusse contentata di por quel luogo in mano di una terza persona confidente anbe le parti, perche lo conservassi a che fusse stato legitimo et Catolico Re di Francia, come da Sua Maesta ella ne fu richiesta, che si saria rimediato a molti inconvenienti et non sariano nati li a[ccidenti].**
translation: ...my predecessor and in my own time. And if Your Highness had initially agreed to put that fortress in the hands of a third person trusted by both sides, to preserve it for whoever became the legitimate Catholic King of France, as His Majesty had requested, many difficulties could have been remedied and those incidents would not have arisen.
